messages:
tara: Heads-up: ACME asked for per-route cost breakdown + span-level tracing hooks for their compliance audit. They want something demonstrable in the next monthly release window.
omar: Do we have a minimal surface we can ship that satisfies their audit without pulling in full tracing UI? :thinking_face:
kesha: Minimal = (1) per-route token/cost table in the route details panel, (2) a sampled span export to S3/OTLP for customers with private deployments.
maria: +1 on sampled export. For hosted we should avoid retaining raw spans in prod UI for privacy/compliance reasons.
james: Can we get the per-route cost table from existing telemetry? We already emit token counts per request to metrics.
kesha: Yep — token_count, model_variant, route_id already exist. Missing piece is route attribution in the datadog traces -> needs a small header propagated and a tag in the ingestion pipeline.
tara: Timebox idea: ship per-route cost table only (no trace UI) in v1. If customers request deeper tracing we offer sampled OTLP export as an enterprise toggle.
omar: Sounds reasonable. What are acceptance criteria for per-route cost table? We need something product can sign off on.
maria: Proposed acceptance criteria:
```
- Per-route panel shows: route_id, 7d token_count, 7d cost_estimate (USD), avg_latency_p95, error_rate
- Numbers reflect only served tokens (not queued/batched duplicates)
- Data freshness <= 15m for hosted
- Tests: unit + e2e that validate aggregation correctness for edge cases (zero tokens, retried requests)
```
james: Also add: must handle routes with multiple model variants (show breakdown or combined?). I'd prefer breakdown by model_variant with expandable rows.
kesha: Expandable rows is a nice-to-have. For MVP we'll show combined and surface a "variant breakdown" button that queries ad-hoc (not pre-aggregated) to avoid expensive rolling counters.
tara: Cost math: use current pricing config for hosted. Document caveat: estimates use on-the-fly price map, not committed discounts for Dedicated customers.
omar: For Dedicated/Private we should expose the raw token counts and let customers map to their pricing. Make that explicit in UI copy.
maria: Risk: if we misattribute tokens we could show negative cost delta customers will notice. Mitigation: show `estimated` tag and include a one-click export CSV for audits.
james: What about tracing hooks? To reduce scope, we implement a light-weight header propagation change and a sampling toggle. Implementation tasks:
- add header x-rd-route-id on internal requests
- add x-rd-sample-span boolean header when sampling enabled
- hook OTLP exporter to customer-configured endpoint
kesha: I'll own headers + ingestion mapping. Omar can own UI and API contract. Tara will own customer communication and acceptance sign-off.
tara: Timeline check: two-week spike to prototype headers + metrics, then two sprints for UI + infra. Is that acceptable for the monthly release window?
omar: Two sprints is tight but doable if we cut the variant breakdown and CSV export to post-launch.
james: We'll also need QA on concurrency / batching to ensure token counts don't double-count with KV cache hits.
maria: Ops ask: include rollout plan with feature-flag and 1% -> 10% -> 100% ramp. Also ensure an alert if cost_estimate delta > 25% vs baseline after rollout.
deploy-bot: Canary started: feature-flag=per-route-cost v1 at 1% in prod (canary id: 2026-03-21-rc1)
kesha: Nice. After canary we should run the comparison job for sample customers and validate counts. I'll add a smoke test.
tara: OK — decision: ship per-route cost table MVP + sampling/OTLP export behind enterprise flag. Post-launch: variant-breakdown + CSV + automated audit report.
omar: I'll update roadmap ticket and remove variant-breakdown from M1 scope. Ticket -> PROD-8473
james: I'll add a short dev checklist in the ticket for batching/kv caveats.
maria: I'll draft the customer-facing note and compliance FAQ after the canary passes.
tara: Thanks team. If no objections by EOD we'll commit the scope. :thumbsup:
